payload.name: PreciseObjectForMissingPreferenceAnswers
payload.description: When a question asks what a person misses, longs for, or finds lacking in a place, use the exact object named in a directly relevant retrieved memory rather than a broader synonym.
content: When a user asks what X misses/longs for/lacks in a location, first check whether any retrieved memory states the missed object explicitly (e.g., 'X misses nature').
If such an explicit statement exists, answer with that specific object (or a close paraphrase of it) instead of a broader category that the same evidence might also imply.
If no retrieved memory names the object explicitly, proceed with the usual synthesis from multiple memories; do not force an unstated object.

solves: When answering what someone misses, longs for, or finds lacking in a place, the model may answer with a broader synonym even though a retrieved memory directly states the exact missed object, causing a mismatch with the expected precise answer. This Skill applies to user questions explicitly asking what a person misses/wants/lacks in a setting, whenever a retrieved memory contains a direct statement of the missed object. It does not apply when no such direct statement exists and the answer must be synthesized from multiple indirect memories.
